title: Open a can with a hand-held rotary opener: one hand keeps the handles squeezed while the other turns the key
instruction: Open the can with the can opener: clamp it on the rim, turn the key until the lid is cut all the way round, then take the opener off and put it on the table.
context: Opening a food can with a hand-held can opener is something most people have done at home. The opener has to be set on the rim with its handles open and squeezed shut, which pierces the lid and clamps the rim between the cutting wheel and the toothed feed wheel; then one hand keeps squeezing while the other turns the wing key, half a turn per grasp, about fourteen times, until the can has turned once under the head. Not stated: the handles spring open when let go, the wheels then leave the rim and turning the key cuts nothing, so one gripper must hold the squeeze the whole time while the other regrasps the key. Unlike popping a crown cap on a mounted opener or prying a tin lid (one lever action), or cutting a held cord or loaf with a blade, here a hand tool must be clamped on the object, kept clamped by one hand, and driven round by the other in many regrasped turns.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). Food can: a standard steel 300 x 407 can (the common "15 oz" size of canned beans or vegetables), 7.6 cm across the rolled double seam at the top (body 7.3 cm), 11.3 cm tall, 0.47 kg full; tinplate lid 3 mm below the top of the seam; red paper label with a cream vertical stripe 1.2 cm wide facing the robot. It stands upright, free, centred at x 42, y -4. Can opener: an ordinary hand-held two-handle rotary opener of the common "swing" pattern (like the Swing-A-Way 407), 0.18 kg. Steel head 4.8 x 2.2 x 3.4 cm carrying a toothed feed wheel 1.2 cm across and, on the upper jaw, a cutting wheel 1.4 cm across; two steel handles 1.6 x 0.9 cm in section and 15 to 16 cm long, with black plastic grips over their rear two thirds, hinged at the head; they open 25 degrees at most and a spring holds them open (holding them shut takes 2.0 N m at the hinge, about 17 N where the gripper holds them 11.6 cm from it; an estimate, not measured). A black wing key 5.5 cm across and 8 mm thick sits on the side of the head on the feed wheel's shaft; one turn of the key turns the rim 0.16 turn past the head (feed wheel 6 mm, rim 37.5 mm in radius). The opener lies flat on the table, key up, handles open and pointing left (+y), its head at x 30, y 10. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Judged from the video and a final photo, with a ruler. The cut: the rim is tracked in 2-degree steps; a step is cut only while the opener is clamped on the rim and the key is turned clockwise (seen from its end) so that the rim passes the cutting wheel. Clamped means the head was set on the rim (within 3 mm radially and in height, 6 mm along the rim, 8 degrees tilt) with the handles at least 20 degrees open and then squeezed within 3 degrees of shut; opened more than 6 degrees, the wheels leave the rim. Turning the key with the handles open, or the wrong way, cuts nothing. The lid stays fixed until every step is cut, then drops loose onto the contents, about 6 mm lower (visible in the video and photo). Score: 0 if the can was ever tipped more than 30 degrees. Otherwise 1.0 (success, held 1 s) if the lid is cut all the way round, the opener is off the can and lying still on the table (lowest point within 1.5 cm of the table, its body nowhere higher than 8 cm, at least 1 cm from the can), the can is upright within 10 degrees and within 5 cm of where it started, and both grippers are at least 2 cm from the opener and the can; 0.75 if the lid is cut all the way round but the opener is still on the can or held; 0.5 if at least half of the rim is cut; 0.25 if the opener was clamped on the rim (the lid pierced); otherwise 0. A real-world judge checks the cut with simple tools: cut all the way round means the lid is free and can be lifted out; for a partial cut, the length of opened seam is measured round the lid's edge with a tape as a share of the full way round, or the can's turn under the head is read from the stripe on its label.
reset_notes: Stand a new sealed can at its mark with the stripe toward the robot. Lay the opener flat at its mark, key up, handles open and pointing left.
fidelity: Rigid bodies (PhysX), 20 Hz control. Metal cutting is not simulated: while the handles are squeezed shut on the seated head, a joint about the can's axis holds opener and can, and its drive turns the can past the head at the feed wheel's ratio as the key turns; rim that passes the cutting wheel counts as cut, and a fixed joint holds the lid until all of it is cut. This clamp joint can lift the can about 2 mm. Estimates: handle spring, key effort, opener mass 0.18 kg, empty can 50 g.
